title: Verifier-executed batched-amplitude tensor-network compiler
difficulty_explanation: Each seeded case has a 64-qubit permuted 8-by-8 interaction grid, 112 opaque RZZ sources in four disjoint matchings, 64 opaque site sources, 64 opaque internal variables, and 48 shuffled output requests. A valid artifact must recover six exact shared-prefix groups, preserve one eight-valued output-lane hyperedge in every group, choose two allowed slices, synthesize a complete 62-variable elimination path under tight live-entry/intermediate/FMA caps, maintain exact evolving operand provenance, and certify the canonical serialization. The solver receives no numerical amplitude target and cannot satisfy functional scoring with amplitude constants because the verifier executes the program on a second fresh tensor realization after the solver has exited.
solution_explanation: The compact expert constructs the full circuit with TensorCircuit, extracts and validates all RZZ endpoints through Circuit.to_qir, derives opaque factor scopes from that native IR, forms the six maximal eight-lane prefix groups, and searches admissible slice pairs with a deterministic frontier-aware elimination compiler. The public instruction defines gates, factor and bytecode semantics, and exact resource arithmetic but does not disclose that search recipe or a winning slice/path.
verification_explanation: The evaluator never imports TensorCircuit. It validates exact built-in types, case identity, every opaque source/query/index ID, batched-lane groups, slices, live operand sets, temporaries, terminal factors, digest, and independently recomputed resources. Only after a subprocess has run the untrusted solution twice and exited does the parent construct both declared and fresh verifier-owned unitary tensors, execute all six groups and four slices, and compare every amplitude lane with an independent 8-row transfer contraction. Separate six-qubit dense-state and three-factor sliced-bytecode canaries validate the factor and executor conventions.

lifecycle.note: These four files are design evidence only. No frozen registry, discussion log, canonical task, safe runner, Docker image, Harbor configuration, or model setting was changed.

contract.resource_model: Exact live tensor entries, exact maximum tensor entries, and the instruction-declared symbolic complex-FMA model are independently replayed from live scopes. Runtime is reported separately and is not inferred from the FMA certificate.
contract.oracle: Independent complex128 row-transfer contraction on declared and fresh post-subprocess unitary tensors, plus separate dense-state and symbolic-bytecode canaries

seed_protocol.mismatch_policy: If both --seed and ORBIT_Q_CANDIDATE_SEED are present they must be identical; disagreement is rejected before submission import.
seed_protocol.base_seed_mapping: One NumPy Generator stream emits the physical layout, opaque variable/site/gate/query/case IDs, every local and RZZ angle, six unique common prefixes, 48 unique suffixes, query shuffle, slice candidates, and nonce.
seed_protocol.case_identity: SHA-256 of sorted-key compact allow_nan-false JSON over the complete exact public config before case_digest is inserted. The evaluator's first stdout line is one full orbit_q_case_identity JSON object containing problem_id, protocol_seed, opaque case_id, and the 64-hex case_digest.
seed_protocol.determinism_scope: Exact case bytes are bound to the target NumPy/runtime and full case_digest; a seed alone is not cross-runtime identity.
seed_protocol.holdout_status: No private holdout is frozen. Every seed and digest listed below is a contaminated public development canary.

isolation_protocol.phase_one: The parent writes only the public config. Two separately launched child processes each scrub seed/key/token/secret/password environment names and sys.argv before importing the submission, invoke run_solution once, reject non-built-in artifact value types before JSON normalization, emit only JSON, and exit. The pristine parent compares canonical JSON for determinism. Child stdout and stderr are discarded rather than trusted as protocol output.
isolation_protocol.phase_two: Each child runs in a new process group; the parent sends SIGKILL to that group after handoff, validates the symbolic artifact, and only then materializes the declared and fresh verifier-owned tensor sets. Those numerical tensor objects never exist in an ordinary worker process.
isolation_protocol.privacy_boundary: This is best-effort subprocess/process-group separation, not a secret-holdout or OS-security proof. A hostile descendant that deliberately escapes its session/process group is not contained, the fresh-angle derivation is deterministic public development logic, and no private key is claimed. Container/VM isolation and artifact freezing still require review before private execution.

difficulty_levers: the dense 64-qubit state has 2^64 amplitudes, while exact row transfer remains feasible at grid width eight
six groups must retain one genuine eight-lane hyperedge rather than compiling 48 independent scalar paths
24 common output bits per group must be factored out without losing opaque query ordering
two slice variables are selected from eight opaque central candidates and affect frontier width and total FMA cost
all 176 source identities and 64 internal-variable identities are seed-scrambled and must remain provenance-correct through 62 destructive elimination steps
live-entry, intermediate, operation, and FMA claims are recomputed from submitted scopes rather than compared with stale solver certificates
fresh post-subprocess tensor execution makes numerical amplitude constants irrelevant even though the public circuit parameters are available
the 160-line expert ceiling couples TensorCircuit QIR extraction, grouping, slicing, path construction, canonicalization, and certificates
anti_shortcut_mutants: a group with no eight-valued batch lane
claim_boundary: This is a deterministic synthetic compiler diagnostic for one declared family: local rotations around a four-layer diagonal RZZ grid. It validates exact amplitudes of that family and a constant-free symbolic execution artifact; it does not establish a general quantum-circuit compiler, an optimal contraction path, a hardware runtime model, or secrecy against an adversarial operating-system process. The resource FMA formula is a benchmark accounting model, not measured wall-clock cost. Local semantic-shim evidence proves expert control flow against the documented QIR surface only. Real TensorCircuit, the pinned image, Harbor, private qualification, and solver-model hardness have not been tested, so the honest admission decision is HOLD.

local_static_validation.mutant_digest_policy: Every semantic artifact mutant refreshes program_digest before validation. Each fails its targeted schema/provenance/lane/slice/step/terminal rule before certificates could act as a stale proxy; the separate false-cost mutant leaves the core and digest valid and fails independent resource recomputation.
local_static_validation.runtime_scope: Final-byte sequential/default and concurrent host self-tests including case construction, two expert invocations, declared and fresh trusted executions, two canaries, all artifact mutants, two-worker determinism/type checks, and ordinary-descendant cleanup; not a pinned TensorCircuit runtime measurement.
hostile_isolation_regressions: child monkeypatch of __main__._canonical cannot forge parent-side determinism
integer subclass is rejected in the worker before JSON normalization
ordinary inherited-process-group descendant is killed before trusted tensor construction
local_static_validation.session_escaping_descendant_status: not contained by this design-only subprocess protocol; explicit promotion blocker requiring container/VM or equivalent task-level teardown
local_static_validation.isolated_semantic_shim_scope: A temporary API-only module exercised the actual two-worker handoff, parent-side determinism comparison, stdout/stderr suppression, process-group cleanup, declared/fresh execution, and first-line identity on seed 1212026. The temporary module was removed and is not one of the bundle files.
local_static_validation.semantic_expert_shim_scope: The host has no TensorCircuit installation. A minimal in-process Circuit/QIR shim checked the expert's documented method calls, ordering, topology extraction, grouping, compiler, and certificates. It is not TensorCircuit execution evidence.

admission_blockers: These exact four files have a separately hashed post-snapshot design_only provenance binding. That lifecycle is provenance-only and the safe runner must reject it before any expert or model path; the frozen snapshot remains unchanged. Execution requires a future separately hashed, human-reviewed executable-promotion contract, and no direct Docker/Harbor bypass is authorized.

Run the exact expert under the pinned TensorCircuit image only after promotion approval. Verify Circuit.rzz and Circuit.to_qir names/index ordering, QIR record count, complex128 setup, runtime below the strict expert gate, and memory on at least 25 freshly frozen expert-only cases.

Replace development process separation with a reviewed artifact-freeze and container/VM protocol before claiming private hidden-tensor isolation. The solution process must be unable to inspect parent memory, future mounts, verifier keys, or private case material.

Freeze a private seed schedule and exact pinned case digests only after the generator, resource caps, tolerance, and two-phase verifier have independent human sign-off. Published development seeds cannot be reused.

Perform authenticated functional, static-policy, and LLM-policy audits. Functional bytecode checks cannot prove TensorCircuit was central because the public config necessarily contains the same topology; source audit must reject a config-only or alternate-framework compiler.

Audit hardness against simple min-fill, row/column sweep, and generic einsum-path baselines. The local expert proves feasibility only; it does not show that the problem resists GPT-5.6 or another solver.

Review whether 8-by-8 diagonal RZZ factorization is scientifically broad enough for admission or should remain a narrow compiler canary. Any gate-family or scale change requires new separately hashed bytes and renewed canaries/caps.

Human reviewers must sign the gate ordering, bit/index convention, prefix factoring, shared-lane hyperedge, slice summation, live-memory and FMA accounting, relative tolerance, exact-type policy, and claim boundary.
exploitability_risks: The edge list is public alongside the circuit, so a submission can reconstruct topology without actually consulting TensorCircuit. Functional scoring cannot distinguish that shortcut; static and LLM source policy are mandatory.
The complete evaluator and development seeds are public. They are design canaries, not private anti-hardcoding evidence.
Many contraction paths may fit the 8-percent cap. The contract intentionally accepts any canonical valid path under the envelope and makes no uniqueness or global-optimality claim.
Fresh tensor values prevent artifact constants but are deterministically derived by public verifier code. Their security value is temporal isolation and semantic mutation, not secrecy.
A hostile child process is not proven contained by subprocess alone. Promotion requires OS-level isolation and frozen artifact transfer.
numerical_statistical_risks: Typical 64-qubit amplitudes are small, so comparison uses per-group maximum-amplitude relative error rather than a unit absolute scale. Zero or constant output would have relative error near one and fail.

Different valid elimination orders can accumulate roundoff differently. The local declared/fresh maximum is about 2e-14 against a 2e-10 relative gate, but pinned BLAS/runtime parity is still required.
The symbolic FMA model counts benchmark operations and ignores backend-specific fusion, sparsity, allocation, and memory traffic.
NumPy Generator bytes can drift across versions; full digest and pinned NumPy identity are mandatory.
api_risks: The expert assumes TensorCircuit's QIR records expose lower-case rzz names and tuple-like index fields in application order.

Circuit.rzz must implement exp(-i theta ZZ/2) and to_qir must retain all 112 endpoints without compiler rewriting; the expert uses QIR for topology but the local shim cannot establish numerical convention.
TensorCircuit backend and dtype settings are process global. The expert requests NumPy and complex128, but this has not been exercised in the target image.
A TensorCircuit release that changes QIR contents or adds implicit records can invalidate the expert's strict record-count check.
